response.cue_rationale: “Pupil of the eye” clearly identifies the anatomical dark opening, and both answers fit that exact sense.

preference_risk.rationale: “Pupil” is plausibly ordinary in both varieties, though Malaysian everyday usage can prefer “anak mata.”

response.rationale: Both forms denote the dark central opening of the eye. Indonesian commonly uses “pupil,” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “anak mata”; this is a useful everyday usage contrast, with “pupil” remaining a formal or technical alternative in Malaysian Malay.
response.risk_rationale: Register affects the Malaysian preference: “pupil” may be more common in medical or formal contexts.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Pupil” is also understood and used in Malaysian Malay, especially formally or technically, but “anak mata” remains a credible ordinary Malay preference; this does not erase the useful contrast.
